doc.title: Jerry Bergonzi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 7, 2022

title: Handling distractions: noisy clubs and Hal Galper
summary: He ignores noisy audiences and concentrates on the music, recalling Hal Galper stopping the band to address talkers.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Can you imagine being in a situation and you’re improvising and you are distracted. Let’s say you’ve parked your car for wherever this gig is and you think it could be towed away. Do you have a way to not let that kind of interference interfere with you?
Well if it came to my car being towed away no.
Okay. Let me dial back on that. There’s someone noisy at the bar.
“Excuse me, man, I’ve got to move my car.” You know? A solo I could do anytime but getting your car towed? I’m going to take care of business.
Okay. I guess what I’m after is you know noisy nightclub.

Oh yeah. I don’t even pay attention to them. My attitude is you don’t bother me, I don’t bother you. Some people get really annoyed. We used to play with Hal Galper. He’d stop the band and he’d get on the microphone and say, “I can hear you, can you hear me?” And I get that. That’s his way to do it. For me I’d just concentrate more on the music. If these people are spending money to come, if they want to talk go ahead. It’s just personally as long as — I hope it’s not too loud but even if it is probably you start playing louder.
Of course the people that are complaining have sat right down in front of the band.
Yeah. And they are clueless. They think that yeah, this is cool, I’m talking. I’m trying to have a conversation here. What’s he doing up there playing? I get it.
